name: StanceThemeProvider
summary: Applies the Stance theme at the app root, persists the preference and avoids a wrong-theme flash at launch.
accessibility: System mode follows the colour scheme and Increase Contrast
Preference is read before the first frame

name: stanceTheme(_:)
summary: Modifier that applies a Stance appearance (system, light, dark or high contrast) to a view hierarchy.
accessibility: Sets tint, foreground and canvas background from tokens

name: stanceScopedTheme(_:)
summary: Scopes a fixed theme to a subtree, for inverted sections and side-by-side previews.
accessibility: Scoped themes keep the same verified contrast as page themes

name: StanceAppearance
summary: The appearance preference with the same stored values as the web: system, light, dark and high-contrast.
accessibility: Increase Contrast resolves system mode to high contrast

name: StanceCard
summary: A padded surface with optional title, description and footer for grouped, self-contained content.
accessibility: Title is exposed as a heading

name: stanceCard()
summary: Modifier that gives any view the card treatment: padding, surface colour, border and optional elevation.
accessibility: High contrast replaces the shadow with a solid outline

name: stanceSurface()
summary: Modifier that places a view on a token surface level with a corner radius, border and optional shadow.
accessibility: Boundaries meet 3:1 contrast in every theme

name: stanceShadow()
summary: Modifier that adds a token elevation; high contrast draws depth as an outline instead of a blur.
accessibility: Depth never relies on subtle shading in high contrast

name: StanceDivider
summary: A hairline separator in the theme separator colour, horizontal or vertical, hidden from VoiceOver.
accessibility: Decorative: hidden from assistive technology

name: StanceSection
summary: A titled group of content with consistent spacing and an optional caption under the heading.
example: StanceSection("Details", caption: "Shown to your organisation") { Text("Body") }
accessibility: Title is exposed as a heading for rotor navigation

name: StanceContainer
summary: Constrains content to a readable width with page gutters and centres it on iPad.
accessibility: Keeps line length readable at every size class

name: StanceGrid
summary: An adaptive grid that fits as many columns as the minimum item width allows.
accessibility: Reflows to one column at large text sizes

name: StanceIcon
summary: A Stance icon drawn natively from the shared icon geometry; decorative unless a label is given.
accessibility: Hidden from VoiceOver without a label
Scales with Dynamic Type

name: stanceText(_:)
summary: Modifier that applies a semantic Stance text style which scales with Dynamic Type and Bold Text.
accessibility: Scales through the largest accessibility sizes
Never below 12pt at the default size

name: StanceButton
summary: A button with six variants, three sizes, icons, a pill shape and a loading state that blocks repeat taps.
accessibility: 44pt minimum target at every size
Loading is announced as “In progress”

name: StanceButtonStyle
summary: The Stance button style for any Button, Menu label or NavigationLink: .buttonStyle(.stance(.primary)).
accessibility: Press feedback respects Reduce Motion

name: StanceIconButton
summary: An icon-only button that requires an accessibility label and keeps a 44pt touch target.
accessibility: Label is required and used by VoiceOver and Voice Control
Pointer hover effect on iPad

name: StanceButtonGroup
summary: Lays related buttons out in a row and stacks them vertically at accessibility text sizes.
accessibility: Reflows instead of truncating at large text sizes

name: StanceMenu
summary: The native Menu with a Stance button as its trigger, for short lists of actions.
accessibility: System menu behaviour, VoiceOver and keyboard support

name: StanceFormField
summary: Wires a visible label, helper text and an announced error message to a single control.
accessibility: Label becomes the control’s accessibility label
Errors are announced when they appear

name: StanceTextField
summary: A labelled single-line text field with helper text, error state, required marker and leading icon.
example: StanceTextField("Template name", text: $text, helper: "Visible to your organisation", isRequired: true)
accessibility: Visible label matches the accessibility label for Voice Control
Error replaces the helper in the hint

name: StanceSecureField
summary: A password field with a show and hide control that keeps a 44pt target.
accessibility: Toggle is labelled Show password or Hide password

name: StanceTextEditor
summary: A labelled multi-line editor with an optional live character count.
accessibility: Character count is part of the field hint

name: StanceSearchField
summary: An inline search field with a clear button; use the system searchable modifier for screen-level search.
accessibility: Clear button is labelled and reachable

name: StancePicker
summary: A labelled native Picker shown as a menu inside Stance field chrome.
accessibility: Selected value is exposed as the accessibility value

name: StanceCheckbox
summary: A checkbox with a label and description; iOS has no system checkbox, so it is exposed as a toggle.
example: StanceCheckbox("Apply to new members", description: "Added later", isOn: $isOn)
accessibility: Whole row is the 44pt target
Announces Checked or Not checked

name: StanceRadioGroup
summary: A group of mutually exclusive options visible at once, with optional descriptions.
accessibility: Selected option carries the selected trait
Group is labelled by its title

name: StanceToggleStyle
summary: Stance colours for the native Toggle switch, keeping system behaviour and accessibility.
accessibility: Native switch semantics and haptics

name: StanceSlider
summary: A labelled native Slider that reports a formatted value visually and to VoiceOver.
accessibility: Adjustable trait with a readable value

name: StanceDatePicker
summary: A labelled native DatePicker for dates or times in Stance colours.
accessibility: System picker with full VoiceOver and keyboard support

name: StanceAdaptiveNavigation
summary: Top-level navigation that is a tab bar in compact width and a sidebar in regular width.
example: StanceAdaptiveNavigation("Stance", selection: $role, destinations: [.init(id: "admin", title: "Home", systemImage: "house")]) { _ in Text("Home") }
accessibility: System bars keep their materials, including Liquid Glass on iOS 26

name: stanceNavigationChrome()
summary: Modifier that themes navigation and tab bar tint while leaving system bar materials untouched.
accessibility: Bar content stays legible in all three themes

name: StanceStepper
summary: Shows progress through a multi-step task with completed, current and upcoming steps.
accessibility: Each step reads “Step x of y” with its state

name: StancePageIndicator
summary: Dots that show the position in a short paged sequence.
accessibility: Read as “Page 2 of 4”
Animation respects Reduce Motion

name: StanceBadge
summary: A short status label in a neutral, info, success, warning or danger tone, always with text.
accessibility: Never colour alone
Outlined in high contrast

name: StanceTag
summary: A keyword label with an optional remove button labelled with the tag name.
accessibility: Remove button reads “Remove Sales”

name: StanceAvatar
summary: A person or organisation shown as an image or initials, in three sizes.
accessibility: Name is the accessibility label

name: StanceAvatarGroup
summary: Overlapping avatars with a +N overflow, read as one summary by VoiceOver.
accessibility: Reads names followed by “and N more”

name: StanceProgressView
summary: Linear or circular progress in Stance colours, determinate or indeterminate.
accessibility: Label and percentage are exposed to VoiceOver

name: StanceSkeleton
summary: A placeholder for loading content in text, circle or rectangle shapes; static under Reduce Motion.
accessibility: Hidden from VoiceOver

name: StanceEmptyState
summary: Explains an empty screen or list and offers the next action.
example: StanceEmptyState(title: "No templates yet", message: "Create your first signature template.") { StanceButton("New template") {} }
accessibility: Title is a heading

name: StanceTimeline
summary: A vertical sequence of events with a title, detail, time and tone.
example: StanceTimeline([.init(id: "1", title: "Deployed", detail: "48 mailboxes", time: "09:41", tone: .success)])
accessibility: Each event is one combined element

name: StanceStatCard
summary: A key figure with a label and a change that is described in words for VoiceOver.
accessibility: Reads “up 12% from last month”, not just an arrow

name: StanceDescriptionList
summary: Term and detail pairs that stack vertically at accessibility text sizes.
accessibility: Each pair is read together

name: StanceListRow
summary: A list row with leading content, title, subtitle and trailing accessory for List and NavigationLink.
accessibility: 44pt minimum row height

name: stanceListStyle()
summary: Modifiers that put List and Form on the Stance canvas with themed rows and separators.
accessibility: Keeps native list behaviour, swipe actions and editing

name: StanceDisclosureGroupStyle
summary: Stance styling for the native DisclosureGroup with a 44pt header.
accessibility: Announces Expanded or Collapsed

name: StanceInlineAlert
summary: An inline status message with a tone icon, title, message and optional actions.
example: StanceInlineAlert("Relay offline", message: "Deployments will resume.", tone: .warning)
accessibility: Warning and danger tones are announced when shown

name: StanceBanner
summary: A full-width announcement with an optional action and dismiss button.
example: StanceBanner("Maintenance on Sunday", actionTitle: "Details", action: {}, onDismiss: {})
accessibility: Dismiss button is labelled and 44pt

name: StanceToastCenter
summary: Queues transient messages, shows one at a time and announces each to VoiceOver.
accessibility: Announced without moving focus
Manual dismiss always available

name: StanceLoadingState
summary: A centred progress indicator with a message for loading screens and regions.
accessibility: Indicator and message are one element

name: StanceErrorState
summary: Explains a failure in plain language and offers a retry action.
example: StanceErrorState(message: "We could not load your templates.") {}
accessibility: Title is a heading; retry is a labelled button

name: stanceSheet()
summary: Presents the native sheet with a title bar, detents and themed content.
accessibility: System sheet gestures, grabber and focus handling

name: stanceAlert()
summary: Presents the system alert from a typed confirmation, with a destructive option.
accessibility: System alert semantics and focus

name: stanceConfirmationDialog()
summary: Presents the system confirmation dialog: an action sheet on iPhone and a popover on iPad.
accessibility: Cancel is always available

name: StanceFilterBar
summary: A horizontally scrolling row of selectable filter chips with a clear-all action.
accessibility: Selected chips carry the selected trait and a check mark

name: StanceSearchableList
summary: A list with native search that filters as you type and announces the result count.
accessibility: Result count is announced
Empty state explains what to try

name: StanceCalendar
summary: A month calendar built on the native graphical DatePicker in Stance colours.
accessibility: Full system calendar accessibility

name: StanceSignatureCanvas
summary: A canvas for drawing a signature with a finger or Apple Pencil, with undo, clear and an alternative slot.
example: StanceSignatureCanvas(signature: $signature) { StanceTextField("Or type your name", text: $text) }
accessibility: Direct-touch trait for VoiceOver
Offer the typed alternative for people who cannot draw

name: StanceAttachmentPicker
summary: Buttons that open the system photo picker and file importer without requesting library permission.
accessibility: System pickers are fully accessible

name: StanceDocumentPreview
summary: Previews a local PDF, image or document with the system Quick Look viewer (iOS only).
accessibility: Quick Look provides zoom, VoiceOver and text selection

name: stanceTouchTarget()
summary: Modifier that guarantees the 44 by 44 point minimum interactive target without changing visual size.
accessibility: Apple HIG minimum target

name: StanceUIKit
summary: UIKit access to Stance: dynamic UIColor roles, Dynamic Type UIFonts and a themed hosting controller.
accessibility: Dynamic colours follow dark mode and Increase Contrast

name: StanceHaptics
summary: Haptic feedback helpers for selection, success, warning and error; no-ops where unavailable.
accessibility: Haptics supplement, never replace, visible feedback

name: StanceThread
summary: The scrolling container for a conversation. Follows the latest message while the reader is at the bottom and releases when they scroll up.
accessibility: A labelled container for the conversation
Never moves the reader while they are scrolled up
Scroll to latest button keeps a 44pt target

name: StanceMessage
summary: One turn in a conversation from the user, the assistant or the system, with slots for actions and a footer.
example: StanceMessage(role: .assistant, status: .streaming, author: "Assistant") { StanceStreamingText(text, isStreaming: true) }
accessibility: Named by author and time
Status is exposed as a value and marked as updating while streaming
The assistant is identified by the sparkle and its name, never by colour

name: StanceMessageGroup
summary: Consecutive messages from one author under a single avatar and name.
accessibility: The group is named by its author
The avatar is decorative

name: StanceMessageActions
summary: The row of actions under a message: copy, retry, edit, good response and bad response.
example: StanceMessageActions(rating: rating, onCopy: {}, onRetry: {}, onRate: { rating = $0 })
accessibility: Every button has a name and a 44pt target
Rating buttons are toggles with a selected state
Copy confirms with a polite announcement
Wraps onto more lines at large text sizes

name: StanceBranchSwitcher
summary: Steps between alternative versions of a message after an edit or retry.
accessibility: Previous and next buttons are named and disabled at the ends
The position is read as "Version 2 of 3" and announced when it changes
Chevrons mirror in right to left layouts

name: StanceScrollToLatest
summary: A floating button that appears when the reader has scrolled away from the newest message.
accessibility: Named "Scroll to latest" with the unread count as its value
44pt target
Fades without movement under Reduce Motion

name: StanceConversationList
summary: A list of past conversations grouped by date, with selection, rename, pin and delete.
example: StanceConversationList([StanceConversation(id: "1", title: "Budget review", updatedAt: date)], selection: $selection, onDelete: { _ in })
accessibility: The open conversation has the selected trait
Rename, pin and delete are swipe actions and context menu items
Section headers name each date group

name: StanceThreadEmptyState
summary: The opening screen of a new conversation with a greeting and starter prompts.
example: StanceThreadEmptyState(description: "Ask about your documents.", starters: [StanceStarter(id: "1", label: "Summarise a file")]) { _ in }
accessibility: The greeting is a heading
Starters are full width buttons with 44pt targets

name: StancePromptComposer
summary: The message input. A text field that grows with its content, with slots for attachments, tools and the send or stop button.
accessibility: A labelled group with a labelled field
Send is disabled when the draft is empty
While a response is generated the same button is named Stop
Controls move below the field at accessibility text sizes

name: StanceAttachmentTray
summary: The attachments on a draft or a sent message: files and images with progress, errors and remove.
accessibility: Each remove button names its file
Upload errors are announced and shown with an icon and text
Becomes a column at accessibility text sizes

name: StanceMentionPicker
summary: A filterable list that opens from a trigger character to reference files, people or tools.
example: StanceMentionPicker(isPresented: $isPresented, query: text, items: [StanceSuggestion(id: "1", label: "Budget.xlsx")]) { _ in }
accessibility: A labelled list above the composer; focus stays in the field
Escape and the VoiceOver escape gesture close it
The number of matches is announced

name: StanceSlashCommandMenu
summary: A command list that opens when the draft starts with a slash.
example: StanceSlashCommandMenu(isPresented: $isPresented, query: text, commands: [StanceSlashCommand(id: "1", name: "summarise")]) { _ in }
accessibility: Same list pattern as the mention picker
Escape and the VoiceOver escape gesture close it

name: StanceModelPicker
summary: Chooses the model for the next message, with a short description and capability badges.
accessibility: The system menu, with its own tick and VoiceOver behaviour
The chosen model is the value

name: StanceContextChips
summary: Shows what the assistant can see for this message, such as files, pages or selections, each removable.
example: StanceContextChips([StanceContextItem(id: "1", label: "budget.xlsx", icon: .file, kind: "File")], onRemove: { _ in }, onAdd: {})
accessibility: Each remove button names its item
The kind is read before the label
Chips wrap instead of truncating the row

name: StanceVoiceInputButton
summary: A microphone button with idle, listening and processing states and a level indicator.
accessibility: A toggle button with the state as its value
State changes are announced
The level ring is still under Reduce Motion

name: StanceStopButton
summary: Stops a response that is being generated.
accessibility: Named "Stop"
44pt target at every size

name: StanceTokenBudgetMeter
summary: A compact meter of how much of the context or message limit is used, with a warning near the limit.
accessibility: One element with the value in words
The warning is an icon and text, never colour alone
Crossing the warning threshold and the limit is announced once each

name: StanceStreamingText
summary: Reveals text as it arrives at a steady cadence with an optional caret, without reflowing what is already on screen.
accessibility: VoiceOver gets the text once, when it is complete, never token by token
Text appears at once under Reduce Motion
Never takes focus

name: StanceThinkingIndicator
summary: Shows that the assistant is working before any text arrives, with an optional label and elapsed time.
accessibility: The label is announced once when it appears
A still sparkle with the label under Reduce Motion
Elapsed time is the value

name: StanceReasoningDisclosure
summary: A collapsible block for the assistant's reasoning. Open while thinking, collapsed to a summary when done.
accessibility: A button with its expanded state
The summary reads, for example, "Thought for 12 seconds"

name: StanceShimmerText
summary: Text with a slow light sweep for labels of work in progress, such as Searching the web.
accessibility: Plain text to assistive technology
No animation under Reduce Motion
The sweep follows the reading direction

name: StanceGenerationProgress
summary: Progress for longer generations such as images or documents: determinate or indeterminate, with a stage label.
accessibility: One element with the percentage and stage as its value
Stage changes are announced politely
A success haptic when it completes

name: StanceStreamingSkeleton
summary: Placeholder lines for a response that has been requested and has not started.
accessibility: One element named "Loading response"
Still under Reduce Motion

name: StanceInterruptedState
summary: Marks a response that was stopped or failed part way, with retry and continue.
accessibility: Errors and lost connections are announced as alerts; stopped and limit are polite
The reason is an icon and words, never colour alone

name: StanceCitationChip
summary: An inline numbered marker that links a claim to its source and previews it on tap.
example: StanceCitationChip(index: 2, source: StanceSource(id: "1", title: "Quarterly report", url: URL(string: "https://example.com")))
accessibility: Named "Source 2: title"
The preview is a popover on iPad and a sheet on iPhone
44pt target around a small mark

name: StanceSourceList
summary: The sources behind an answer, as a compact row that expands to a full list.
accessibility: The compact row is a button with its expanded state
Each row is a link named by number, title and site

name: StanceSourcePreview
summary: A card for one source: title, site, snippet and a link to open it.
example: StanceSourcePreview(StanceSource(id: "1", title: "Quarterly report", domain: "example.com", snippet: "Revenue grew 12%."))
accessibility: The open control is a link
Text wraps instead of truncating at regular size

name: StanceConfidenceBadge
summary: States how sure the system is in words, never colour alone.
accessibility: The level is always written out
The bars icon is decorative

name: StanceAIGeneratedLabel
summary: Marks content as written or edited by AI.
accessibility: Read as one phrase
Identified by the sparkle and words, not a hue

name: StanceDisclaimerNote
summary: A quiet note under the composer or a response, such as a reminder to check important facts.
accessibility: Muted text still meets contrast in every theme
The icon is decorative

name: StanceFeedbackBar
summary: Thumbs up or down, followed by optional reasons and a comment, then a thank you.
accessibility: Thumbs are toggle buttons
Reasons are a labelled group of toggles
Submission is announced

name: StanceReportDialog
summary: A sheet to report a response with a category and details.
example: Button("Report") { isPresented = true }.stanceReportDialog(isPresented: $isPresented, categories: [StanceReportCategory(id: "wrong", label: "Incorrect")]) { _ in }
accessibility: The system sheet with its own dismissal gestures
Submit is disabled until a category is chosen
Stays open and busy while the report is sent, then announces it

name: StanceSensitiveContentGate
summary: Hides content behind a notice until the reader chooses to see it.
accessibility: Hidden content is not in the accessibility tree
VoiceOver focus moves to the content on reveal
